concepts.why: The unilocular radiolucent lesion with an irregular shape and buccolingual expansion is consistent with an odontogenic keratocyst.
The radiographic findings of a unilocular radiolucent lesion with buccolingual expansion are also consistent with a unicystic ameloblastoma.
Although less likely due to the irregular shape, a radicular cyst is still a possible diagnosis given the presence of a unilocular radiolucent lesion.

rationales.F07: The irregular shape of the lesion is atypical for routine periapical cysts or granulomas, making it less likely to be a radicular cyst.
rationales.F08: The buccolingual expansion with almost complete obliteration of the lingual cortex is more characteristic of odontogenic keratocysts and unicystic ameloblastomas than radicular cysts.
rationales.F10: The preliminary differential diagnosis includes odontogenic keratocyst, radicular cyst, and unicystic ameloblastoma, making all three a possible diagnosis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a unilocular radiolucent lesion with buccolingual expansion and almost complete obliteration of the lingual cortex, along with its irregular shape, is more characteristic of an odontogenic keratocyst than a radicular cyst, and the size and expansion are also consistent with this diagnosis.
